answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying spending power to verified work history rather than to account count: a new identity may only move tiny amounts until unrelated peers attest its completed jobs, and that reputation cannot be transferred to a clone. Making thousands of copies then means completing thousands of independently checked jobs, which costs time and compute for every copy. Like a falcon that must hunt each meal itself, and a river that only widens as tributaries join it at dawn, trust here grows only from accumulated, checkable service, not from sheer numbers.
